newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin sees baht stability in up to 2 months.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin sees baht stability in up to 2 months.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said he expects foreign exchange and Thai interest rate volatility to ease in one to two months following baht flotation on Wednesday.
Thanong said in parliament he was confident that Thai economic and financial sector problems were not insurmountable.
"I believe that the situation has not deteriorated to the point that it is beyond salvation," the minister said.
"I believe that solving problems require courage and knowledge of how to tackle them...I used to be involved in bailing out companies in the April 4 (1984) scheme," Thanong said.
"At that time, problems were attributed to frauds and forged promissory notes but this time, the issue stemmed from deterioration of corporate assets under the current weak economic cycle," he said.

Thanong said he believed that what the government has done in the past week are on the right track in tackling problems. "They will convince the world that Thailand is not bogged down as an undeveloped backwater."

Thanong, a former low-profile banker and chief executive of Thai Military Bank Plc, took over the finance portfolio last month after his predecessor Amnuay Viravan abruptly resigned over policy conflicts with other cabinet ministers.

He spoke in parliament which debated on four government proposed urgent decrees that gave the authorities power to help merge troubled finance firms and to rescue an ailing property sector saddled with a huge glut for several years.
The ruling coalition government late on Wednesday pushed one of the four decrees through the lower House of Representatives where it controlled 222 of its 393 seats.

Most opposition politicians abstained or boycotted the passage of the first decree that amended the Commercial Banking Act. It is not immediately known when the debate on the other decrees would be concluded.
